questions.stem: Which of the following describes the locus of points equidistant from two given points $A$ and $B$?

options.text: A circle with center at $A$
A line parallel to $AB$
The perpendicular bisector of $AB$
A line passing through $A$ and $B$

questions.explanation: The locus of points equidistant from two points is the perpendicular bisector of the line segment joining the points. This line is equidistant from both points at all locations.

distractorRationale.a: A circle centered at $A$ would not be equidistant from $B$.
distractorRationale.b: A line parallel to $AB$ does not maintain equal distance from both points.
distractorRationale.d: A line passing through $A$ and $B$ would not be equidistant from both points.
